primary_topics: Guest of Honor address at the SM Foundation scholar-graduates presentation, May 12, 2009 -- invited by SM Foundation Executive Director-Education Carmen Linda M. Atayde

Henry Sy Sr. as the governing exemplar: CJP's 50-year personal history with SM (from Carriedo Shoemart to the global enterprise); three SYs -- SYnergy (business interrelation), SYmmetry (personal and family life), SYmphony (relation to God and philanthropy)
Three Ps for the scholar-graduates: Patience, Perseverance and Prayers -- all beginning with P as in Panganiban
SM Foundation since 1983: educational, health and medical, mall-based outreaches, livelihood and religious programs for the marginalized
sub_topics: SM enterprise scale (as of 2009): nearly P150 billion in revenues; over 75,000 workers; 100 stores nationwide (34 SM department stores, 25 supermarkets, 14 SaveMore, 13 hypermarkets, 14 Makro); three of the world's biggest malls: SM Mall of Asia, SM Megamall, SM City North EDSA

Mr. Synergy: 'He sticks to his core business and to his area of expertise. Thus, although his business empire seems diversified, it is really inter-related: retail, tourism and entertainment, shopping centers, real estate and banking.'

CJP's first Shoemart purchase: 'I first met Dr. Henry Sy more than fifty years ago, when as a struggling student, I bought my shoes at his Shoemart store in Carriedo Street in Manila at, believe it or not, only ten pesos at that time.'

SYmmetry: personal life -- 'six children who are my teammates and friends in the office and at home'; 'my wife of over fifty years, Molly, who is my lifetime companion, treasurer, adviser and best friend'; 'deep faith in God, who according to him is good and generous with His gifts to us'

God at the center of SM projects: Chapel of the Eucharistic Lord inside SM Megamall; Shrine of Jesus, the Way, the Truth and the Life near Mall of Asia (built before the MOA; in response to Pope John Paul II's wish for a youth center during the 1995 World Youth Day)

SYmphony: 'he was once poor... his passion is not really to accumulate more wealth but to distribute it equitably to the marginalized, the dispossessed, the infirm and the helpless'; SM Foundation since 1983

Three Ps for scholar-graduates: (1) Patience -- 'many times brilliant individuals become maladjusted because they are in so much hurry... patience is a virtue that must be consciously nurtured by the brilliant'; (2) Perseverance -- 'as Thomas Edison once said, Genius is ninety-nine percent perspiration and one percent inspiration. Never give up'; (3) Prayers -- 'Believe that there is a God... Many times, when we do not get what we want, we feel embittered and doubt His power. But our God is infinitely intelligent and powerful. He knows our needs better than we do.'

Synopsis: 'three easy-to-remember acronyms': (1) remember and internalize the three Ps (all beginning with P as in Panganiban); (2) remember the three SYs of Dr. Henry Sy Sr. (SYnergy, SYmmetry, SYmphony)

stances.claim: Henry Sy Sr.'s three SYs -- SYnergy (all businesses interrelated), SYmmetry (family and personal life centered on God and family), SYmphony (philanthropy rooted in remembering his own poverty) -- form a complete model of the entrepreneur-philanthropist that CJP has advocated throughout his FLP work. The SM Foundation embodies the 'help the poor help themselves' philosophy that JGF and FLP both aspire to.
stances.rhetorical_move: three-SYs-as-complete-model: Henry Sy's life as the empirical proof of the integrated entrepreneur-philanthropist that CJP has advocated across the corpus

stances.claim: Patience is the specific virtue that 'the brilliant' most need to consciously nurture -- because brilliance tends toward impatience (being 'in so much hurry'). This is CJP's most counterintuitive leadership lesson: the most talented people need to work hardest at the one virtue they are least likely to have.
stances.rhetorical_move: counterintuitive-patience argument: the brilliant's greatest deficit is patience, making it the most important of the three Ps for the SM scholars specifically

notable_anecdotes: The P10 shoes at Carriedo: 'I first met Dr. Henry Sy more than fifty years ago, when as a struggling student, I bought my shoes at his Shoemart store in Carriedo Street in Manila at, believe it or not, only ten pesos at that time.' -- CJP's most personal connection to an entrepreneurial giant.

God at the center of SM: before building the Mall of Asia, Henry Sy first constructed the Shrine of Jesus, the Way, the Truth and the Life near it -- 'in response to the late Pope John Paul II's wish for a center for the youth during the 1995 World Youth Day.' Even in the biggest commercial complex, the chapel inside Megamall is where shoppers 'can still find peace and tranquility.'

Three Ps as Panganiban: 'if my presence today and my speech will have any meaning for you, let it be two things... remember and internalize my life story of patience, perseverance and prayer. They are all easy to remember because they all begin with P as in Panganiban.' -- the most self-referential mnemonic in the corpus.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 12, 2009 as the Guest of Honor address at the SM Foundation scholar-graduates presentation -- invited by Executive Director-Education Carmen Linda M. Atayde -- this address by CJP structures Henry Sy Sr.'s life around three SYs: SYnergy (his businesses are interrelated despite appearing diversified: retail, tourism/entertainment, shopping centers, real estate, banking; 'he sticks to his core business and to his area of expertise' -- earning him the title 'Mr. Synergy'); SYmmetry (personal and family life: 'six children who are my teammates and friends in the office and at home'; wife Molly of 50+ years as 'lifetime companion, treasurer, adviser and best friend'; 'deep faith in God'); and SYmphony (relation to God and philanthropy: before building the Mall of Asia, he first constructed the Shrine of Jesus near it in response to Pope John Paul II's 1995 World Youth Day wish; the Chapel of the Eucharistic Lord inside Megamall; SM Foundation since 1983 for the marginalized). CJP's personal connection: 'I first met Dr. Henry Sy more than fifty years ago, when as a struggling student, I bought my shoes at his Shoemart store in Carriedo Street in Manila at, believe it or not, only ten pesos.' The SM enterprise today (2009): nearly P150 billion in revenues; 75,000+ workers; 100 stores (34 SM departments, 25 supermarkets, 14 SaveMore, 13 hypermarkets, 14 Makro); three of the world's biggest malls: Mall of Asia, Megamall, SM City North EDSA. For the scholars, CJP offers three Ps: Patience ('many times brilliant individuals become maladjusted in their careers... being too much in a hurry... patience is a virtue that must be consciously nurtured by the brilliant'); Perseverance ('Thomas Edison: genius is 99% perspiration and 1% inspiration'); and Prayers ('God knows our needs better than we do; He will always provide all things good for us, in His own time and in His own way'). Synopsis: 'they are all easy to remember because they all begin with P as in Panganiban.'
